analysis.title: Strong 3Q earnings can send US equities higher (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: UBS CIO expects another solid set of S&P 500 earnings and guidance in the 3Q reporting season, even though September headline inflation could re-accelerate.
UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% for the September quarter, supported by AI demand, an improvement in cyclical segments, and resilient consumer spending.
AI-related spending is estimated to rise 84% this year to USD 900bn. UBS expects semiconductor profits alone to account for about half of S&P 500 earnings growth in 3Q.

UBS expects average hyperscaler cloud revenue growth of 58% y/y for the September quarter, up from 48% in the June quarter. Capex growth is forecast to slow next year, but the investment appears to be paying off.

Higher energy prices are a headwind for businesses exposed to freight costs (retailers, goods manufacturers) and for travel-related companies. UBS thinks the impact on aggregate S&P 500 profits is limited.

The ISM Manufacturing new orders component has been in expansion for nine consecutive months, versus an average expansion of about three years historically. UBS sees a good growth runway for manufacturers and industrials.
Initial jobless claims remain near multi-decade lows, which UBS thinks should prevent a meaningful deterioration in consumer spending despite pressure on lower-end consumers from energy prices.

The 10-year Treasury yield is up more than 1 percentage point this year, but UBS sees refinancing risk for S&P 500 companies as manageable. Non-financial debt has a weighted average maturity of about 11 years.

UBS recommends diversified US equity positioning combining cyclical and secular exposure. Themes are Transformational Innovation Opportunities (AI, Power and resources, Longevity). Sectors liked are financials, industrials, utilities, health care and consumer discretionary.

Asian equities fell on Tuesday led by chipmakers after the Wall Street semiconductor sell-off. The Kospi fell 5.5% (Samsung -7.4%, SK Hynix -10.1%), the Nikkei 225 fell 1.8% and Taiwan's benchmark fell 2%. Headlines pointed to rising memory-chip competition and potential financing constraints in AI infrastructure.

UBS maintains a positive view on Asian equities. It favors Asian tech names with strong earnings visibility (AI chip foundries, the CPU supply chain) and sees opportunities in Japan, India, Singapore and onshore China A-shares.

NY Fed President Williams said one more rate increase may be appropriate this year, but sees no reason to raise again in 2027. He expects inflation to move toward 2% next year as tariff and energy effects fade. Two-year Treasury yields edged lower after his remarks.
Markets currently price a Fed hike in December and two further moves in 2027. UBS's base case is that the Fed waits until December rather than hiking at the 27-28 October meeting.
Wednesday's (14 October) US September CPI is the last inflation report before the Fed's 27-28 October meeting and is key to whether recent inflation progress continues.

tension_points.theme: US equities versus inflation and energy
tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects 28% 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth driven by AI, cyclical improvement and resilient consumers, which leaves room for US equities to rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Headline September CPI could re-accelerate, elevated oil prices hurt freight- and travel-exposed companies, and the 10-year yield is up more than 1 percentage point this year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A September CPI report showing inflation progress has stalled, which could prompt an October Fed hike rather than December.
